extracted.intended_audience: readers/users of the Yearbook index (librarians, editors, researchers, and readers of short fiction)
extracted.subtask_description: Conventions and annotation rules for compiling/reading a yearbook index of short stories published in magazines (how titles, author notes, volume/page references, and periodical abbreviations are presented).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three asterisks indicate permanent literary value / Rolls of Honor
rubrics_metrics.description: Three asterisks prefixed to a title indicate the more or less permanent literary value of the story, and entitle it to a place on the annual "Rolls of Honor."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles in the index that begin with three asterisks (***Title) are being marked as having enduring literary merit and are listed on the annual Rolls of Honor. (Examples in the index: entries shown with '***' before the title.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross references after an author's name
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross references after an author's name refer to previous volumes of this series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an author's entry contains parenthetical cross-references (e.g., "See 1916, 1918"), those direct the reader to the author's appearances in earlier Yearbook volumes. Use these to trace the author's entries across volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: (H.) author note referencing The Standard Index of Short Stories
rubrics_metrics.description: (H.) after the name of an author indicates that other stories by this author, published in American magazines between 1900 and 1914, are to be found indexed in "The Standard Index of Short Stories," by Francis J. Hannigan, published by Small, Maynard & Company, 1918.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An '(H.)' tag after an author's name signals that further bibliographic coverage for that author (specifically, items from 1900–1914) appears in Hannigan's Standard Index. Use this to locate additional earlier works not repeated in the Yearbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parenthetical figures after story titles indicate volume and page
rubrics_metrics.description: The figures in parentheses after the title of a story refer to the volume and page number of the magazine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formats seen include (volume.), (volume:page) and (page) depending on magazine pagination. Examples from the index: '(12.)', '(126:522.)'. These tell the reader where the story appeared in the source magazine (volume and page).

rubrics_metrics.name: When successive magazine numbers are not paged consecutively, give page number only
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases where successive numbers of a magazine are not paged consecutively, the page number only is given in this index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a magazine's issues restart pagination or otherwise do not use continuous page numbering across issues, the index omits the volume and supplies only the page number in parentheses after the title. This explains entries that show only a single number in parentheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sectioning by author nationality / major heading
rubrics_metrics.description: Index is organized under major headings (example: 'I. American Authors'), indicating categorization of entries by author nationality or similar major grouping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Roman-numeral and heading structure (e.g., 'I. American Authors') to navigate the index and locate authors/stories grouped by the given classification.
